label: Macro Rig
description: Working macro setups — optics, magnification and field technique for photographing very small subjects.

items.name: 100mm-lifesize
items.text: a 100mm macro lens at life-size 1:1, the razor-thin focal plane laid exactly through the eyes, everything beyond melting into creamy color
items.text_short: 100mm macro at 1:1, plane on the eyes

items.name: twin-flash-diffused
items.text: twin macro flashes fired through heavy diffusion, wraparound light with tiny jewel speculars, every hair and scale edge cleanly separated from the background

items.name: focus-stack-rail
items.text: a sixty-frame focus stack shot on a rack-and-pinion rail, impossible front-to-back sharpness at high magnification, texture resolved beyond what the eye can see

items.name: probe-lens
items.text: a tubular probe lens threaded in at subject height, bug's-eye wide-angle perspective, the small world curving away huge behind the subject

items.name: reversed-fifty
items.text: a reversed 50mm prime on extension tubes, focus found by leaning in millimeter by millimeter, vintage rendering around one fragile sliver of sharpness

items.name: backlit-low-sun
items.text: shot low against the low sun, wings, hairs and filaments rim-lit into glowing fibers, a deep shaded background keeping the halo clean

items.name: cold-still-tripod
items.text: worked in the first cold light while the subject sits chilled and motionless, tripod and cable release, windless air, dew held mirror-still on every surface
items.text_short: tripod macro on a cold-still subject

items.name: silver-reflector-fill
items.text: one silver reflector held close, field light bounced back into the shadow side, natural single-source modelling with complete readable detail

items.name: ground-pod
items.text: camera on a ground pod at soil level, shooting through the moss horizon, near foreground blur washing the frame edges in soft green

items.name: aperture-slice
items.text: shot nearly wide open for a single knife-edge plane of focus, everything before and behind dissolving into smooth graduated color fields
